rti-01.note: Read The News Minute (27 Sep 2026), The Times of India (31 Aug 2025) and Mathrubhumi (28 Sep 2026). Quote is verbatim in TNM. TOI gives the application date (28 July), the request for time to inspect the files, and the CPIO reply dated 27 August with both quoted sentences verbatim. Mathrubhumi states that the Principal Secretary signed as First Appellate Authority in response to the first appeal, which supports the answer. The note's statement that the applicant posted the appellate reply on X on 24 September 2026 is not on any page read. TNM says only that the reply became a talking point a day after The Indian Express report of 23 September. Names of the applicant and the officer appear on the pages and not in the item.

fix.note: Two stages of one application. The CPIO reply of 27 August 2025 is reported by The Times of India (quote: 'You may refer to Commission's guidelines dated June 24, 2025 which is self- explanatory and available on the Commission's website.' and 'Further, no information in this regard is available in the Commission'). The first appellate reply, signed by the Principal Secretary as First Appellate Authority, is undated in the reports. The News Minute reported it on 27 September 2026 and Mathrubhumi on 28 September 2026. The News Minute also reports that the CPIO had not provided the files 'as the requisite information is not available with him in any material form.'

rti-02.note: Read Deccan Herald (28 Aug 2025) and The Times of India (31 Aug 2025). The quote is verbatim in DH. TOI gives the application date as 28 July and says the CPIO 'just shared the link to the June-24, 2025 guidelines'. Neither outlet dates this reply, so replied stays blank. Neither reports the Commission saying that no record is held or citing an exemption. It sent an unrelated document. 'no record held' therefore overstates what the reply said. Proposed label 'not supplied'. If the outcome vocabulary is closed, 'refused' is the nearer of the existing labels (DH headline: 'refuses to provide'), but it should then carry no section. The Scroll article in also was not opened by this reader.

fix.note: The quote is the outlet's sentence. The reply did not say that no record is held and cited no exemption. It supplied the 2025 guidelines in place of the 2003 order, so the outcome is recorded as not supplied. Scroll reported on 10 July 2025, outside the RTI process, that a Commission official said the 2003 instruction could not be traced.

rti-03.note: Read The Reporters' Collective (29 Aug 2025). The quote is verbatim, including the curly quotation marks around comprehensive instructions. Asked and answer match the page ('failed to acknowledge the existence of such files and records'). The page says the application was filed shortly after the SIR was announced and gives no reply date. 'partly supplied' overstates the reply. Nothing the applicant could open was supplied, and the applicant could not find the 14 July 2025 instructions on the Commission's site either. Same label as rti-02 is proposed.

fix.note: The applicant reports the application was filed shortly after the 24 June 2025 announcement and that it would appeal. No outcome of an appeal was found. The reply pointed to instructions dated 14 July 2025 that the applicant could not open and did not acknowledge any file on the decision, so the outcome is recorded as not supplied.

rti-04.note: Read The Reporters' Collective (29 Aug 2025) and its thread page. Quote verbatim. The Ministry 'claimed it would not have kept records of such consultations and transferred the request to the ECI'. The thread says the Supreme Court hears the case 'tomorrow' on Monday 28 July, so it dates to 27 July 2025, and it says 'We have appealed it'. The Ministry's reply is shown as an image in the thread. It was not transcribed here, and it is the Ministry's reply, not the Commission's of 20 August.

rti-05.note: Read The Reporters' Collective (14 Jul 2026). Quote verbatim and correctly labelled as the outlet's characterisation. The three questions, the transfer to all 38 district election offices, the eleven months, and the two replies (Dulhin Bazar subdivision of Patna, and Hajipur, which the outlet calls a district headquarters and 'the only district that replied') all match. Images of the application and of both replies are on the page. The page names the applicant, the item does not. The '36 of 38' in the note is an inference from the outlet's account, since Dulhin Bazar is a subdivision and not a district office. The Quint lead in not_found (11 August 2025, same activist, applications on Bihar's SIR) is very likely the filing stage of this application, which fits the eleven months.

rti-06.note: Read The Wire (15 Aug 2026). Quote verbatim. Filing 29 November 2025 and reply 19 March 2026 are stated. Two pages of notings, initiated by an Under Secretary on 27 October 2025 and approved the same day, and no minutes supplied, all match. An image of the notings is on the page. The Badarpur refusal under Section 8(1)(j) and the other non-SIR applications are as the note says. The author's name appears in the not_found list (Wire lead), not in any item.

rti-07.note: Read ETV Bharat Bangla (18 Mar 2026). The Bengali quote is verbatim and is the petitioner's lawyer speaking. The page says the High Court directed the officer under the Commission to give the information within seven days, on Wednesday 18 March, by Justice Krishna Rao. The lawyer says the Commission gave no information, the appellate authority directed the CPIO to give it within seven days, and the appellate authority warned on 9 February. The year of 9 February is inferred from context and is consistent. The asked field is a fair reading: the page speaks of infiltrators and foreigners on the roll. A second report was looked for in English and Bengali and not found. The order itself was not found. Single source stands. The page names the petitioner and the lawyer, the item does not.

rti-08.note: Read Deccan Herald (PTI, 24 Sep 2026) and ThePrint Hindi (Bhasha, 24 Sep 2026). Quote verbatim. Both give 'April 17' and 'July 21' without a year. 2026 is the only reading that fits. The application asked for flagged counts 'at the time of final publication of the electoral roll', and West Bengal's final roll was published on 28 February 2026 (ETV Bharat, rti-07), so the application followed it. The reply was then publicised in September 2026. Section 8(1)(d) for points 1 and 2, 'no module has been developed specifically for SIR in West Bengal', and the referral to EROs for the counts all match. Outcome 'refused' with the note 'partly refused and partly answered' is fair. A Facebook post titled 'Saket Gokhale RTI appeal on ECI SIR software secrecy 2026' suggests a first appeal was filed. Not opened, listed as a lead.

rti-09.note: Read The News Minute (15 Aug 2026). The quote matches except the trailing comma, which is the outlet's punctuation before 'the ECI said'. Reply dated 'August 13' with no year, and the article is of 15 August 2026, so 2026 is right. The coalition is named as applicant and says a member filed it. Asked and answer match. No transfer under Section 6(3) is mentioned.

rti-10.note: Read The Wire (25 Aug 2026), The Indian Express (26 Aug 2026) and National Herald (26 Aug 2026). The quote is verbatim in The Wire as the reply's footnote. Memo No. 8551/Home (Elec) dated 17 August 2026, 28 pages, as on 7 August 2026, 38,10,620 received, 82,782 decided, 75,443 included and 7,339 excluded all match The Wire. The restored count is settled by the reply's own table. The Wire's header illustration reproduces the CEO's 'Appellate Tribunal Appeal Report as on 07.08.2026', district by district, with totals 3810620, 75443 and 7339 circled. 75,443 plus 7,339 is 82,782, while 75,339 plus 7,339 is 82,678. National Herald's 75,339 is an error. National Herald also says the reply informed the MP that 31 lakh of the 38 lakh appeals challenged inclusion. The Wire says the reply does not establish who filed the excess appeals, and Indian Express quotes a party petitioner, not the reply, for a 7 lakh figure. Treat the 31 lakh as unconfirmed. The table image is one page of the reply inside an illustration, so it is recorded as doc_url but kind should stay press.

fix.note: The quote is the reply's own footnote as The Wire reports it. The Wire shows images of the application and of the reply's district table as on 7 August 2026, whose totals read 38,10,620 received, 75,443 included and 7,339 excluded. National Herald gives 75,339, which does not add up to 82,782 with 7,339 and is an error. The applicant's press release of 21 August 2026 treats about 10.8 lakh appeals as filed by the Commission, which The Wire says the reply does not establish. National Herald's statement that the reply put 31 lakh appeals against inclusion is not supported by The Wire or The Indian Express.

rti-11.note: Read the Internet Freedom Foundation post (6 Oct 2026). Quote verbatim. Applications to the ECI and the CEOs of Delhi and West Bengal, no filing dates or reference numbers given, and the asked field is a fair summary (logical discrepancy criteria and version history, ERONET 2.0, ECINET and digitisation contracts, Election Commissioners' recorded objections and full Commission minutes, data retention and sharing, State-wise excluded, noticed, deleted and appeal counts). Pending is right.

leads.lead: Two RTI findings on SIR expenditure cited in the CJP online assembly resolution of 3 October 2026. An application on the 'sanctioned budget & expenditure incurred on the SIR Phase 2 (Bihar and 12 other states)' reportedly drew a reference to a 1978 circular splitting costs 50:50 between Centre and State, with no copy of the circular supplied. An earlier application to the CEO Bihar on actual expenditure reportedly drew the reply that districts had not compiled the data.
